phrases.phonetic_text: hala ikhit khalhitsote itsehe
phrases.phonetic_broad: ala ikit kalitsote itsee

phrases.phonetic_broad: l yo yttsiie
phrases.english_text: You didn’t kill them?

phrases.syllabary_text: Mhm ᏥᏔᎦ ᎤᏲᎢᏃ ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᏳᏟᎢᎶᏝ
phrases.phonetic_text: amham tsithaka uyo'in nunalhstanhe tanihstyohihv yul'ilola
phrases.phonetic_broad: amam tsitaka uyoin nunalstane tanistyoiv yulilola
phrases.english_text: Mhm, the chickens. They had it bad when Christmas came.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏩᎦᏲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏁ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: wakayo ohst nnatvn thv
phrases.phonetic_broad: wakayo ost nnatvn tv
phrases.english_text: The cows had it good though?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏌᏌ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏚᏂᎾᏝᎥ ᎾᏅ ᏗᏈᏍᏙ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᎡᏥ Ꮎ ᎤᏄᏱᏔᏅ ᎦᏤᏍᏙ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏙᎩᎾᎥ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohst nuntn sahs skwu tsituninalha'v nn tikwhsto tsitekolhskv etsi na unuythanv ktsehsto skwu tstokina'v skyuhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: ost nuntn sas skwu tsituninalav nn tikwsto tsitekolskv etsi na unuytanv ktsesto skwu tstokinav skyusti
phrases.english_text: They had it good. We also had geese. Mama would make pillows with the feathers, and mattresses too.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎮᏃ ᎦᏌᎴᎾ ᏏᏛᎮ ᏴᏩᏔ ᎪᎯᏥᎩ Ꮎ goose down ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᏔᏅ ᏧᎦᎾᏫ ᎥᏍᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skhen kahsalena sitvhe ywath khitsik na kuhs tan shk yuhst tikolhvthanv tsknwi vhski iyhsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: sken kasalena sitve ywat kitsik na kus tan sk yust tikolvtanv tsknwi vski iysti
phrases.english_text: Jackets today, you can still find them made with goose down. Those that are made like that are really warm.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮᎨ ᏗᎬᏄ
phrases.phonetic_text: itsalhsteliheke tikvnu
phrases.phonetic_broad: itsalstelieke tikvnu
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᎨ ᏴᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: tokhe yta
phrases.phonetic_broad: toke yta
phrases.english_text: Did you all help with… how do you say…

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏗᎬᏄᏯᎩᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: tknuykita
phrases.phonetic_broad: tknuykita
phrases.english_text: Plucking their feathers.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᏦᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎡᎵᏏᎮᏃ ᏗᎯᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᏭᏃ Ꭰ ᏥᏂᏕᎬᏁᎲ ᏥᏓᏍᏆᏄᏖᏲ ᏥᏓᎯᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v tsotslhstelihv elihsihen tihihi tsikehv nawno a tsintekvnehv tstahskwanuthey tsthihv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv tsotslsteliv elisien tiii tsikev nawno a tsintekvnev tstaskwanutey tstiv
phrases.english_text: We helped. Grandma used to kill them and then she went like this [gestures] when she twisted their necks when she killed them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᏔᎦᏛ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏗᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsithkatv utloy the tskhv thv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsitkatv utloy te tskv tv
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏲᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏓᏥᏫᏒᏗ ᏄᏍᏕ ᏍᎩ ᏲᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: yokhe ohst tatsiwhsvt nuhste sk yonhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: yoke ost tatsiwsvt nuste sk yonv
phrases.english_text: Kill chickens the same way back then, ain’t it? Did you all have a good garden back then?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎥᎿᏅ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏃᏭ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎡᎵ ᎣᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎣᎬᏌ ᎣᎩᏍᏚᏟᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭ ᎠᎹ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v vnhanv elt nw katuhs skwu tsuwokiluhtsv eli ohsi tsikehv ahseno okvhsa okihstutlhst tskehv nowu ama
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vnanv elt nw katus skwu tsuwokilutsv eli osi tsikev aseno okvsa okistutlst tskev nowu ama
phrases.english_text: Yes, below. When we got to the mountain it was good, but we had to water it ourselves.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: ttv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ttv
phrases.english_text: You did?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎲ ᎥᎿ ᎨᏓᎵ ᎨᎲ Ᏺ Ꮎ ᏓᏓᏑᎶᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎯᏌᏛᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhv vnha khetli kehv yo na tatahsulohskv ohst tshinkalhsthv na amayulhit kehv ahihsathvhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv vna ketli kev yo na tatasuloskv ost tsinkalstv na amayulit kev aisatvskv
phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, down the hill it would give off dew. By the creek it did really good with the morning dew.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᎢᏨᏁᎮ ᎢᏥᏓᎷᎩᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: to itsvnhe itsitalukihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: to itsvne itsitalukiske
phrases.english_text: How did y’all plow the ground?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏐᏈᎵ ᏥᏓᏅᏗᎲ ᎦᏓᎷᎪᏗ ᏗᏂᎴᏅᎯᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: sokwili tstanhvhtihv katlukoti tinilenvhita
phrases.phonetic_broad: sokwili tstanvtiv katlukoti tinilenvita
phrases.english_text: They used a horse-drawn plow, and donkeys.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏕᏥᎾᏝᎡᎨ ᎩᎶᎨ ᏄᏓᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: tetsinalha'ek khiloke nutle
phrases.phonetic_broad: tetsinalaek kiloke nutle
phrases.english_text: Did you own them or did someone else?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏙ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᎥᏍᎩᎾ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏂᏚᎾᏓᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihsi tskhv ut tsitunalha'v vhskin na'v tsintuntalv
phrases.phonetic_broad: elisi tskv ut tsitunalav vskin nav tsintuntalv
phrases.english_text: Grandma’s brother owned them. They were neighbors.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮩ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏣᏛᏁ
phrases.phonetic_text: t skwu ohst nitsatvnhe
phrases.phonetic_broad: t skwu ost nitsatvne
phrases.english_text: Y’all had it really good there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ika ohst noktvnv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ika ost noktvnv
phrases.english_text: We did really well.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏴᏣᏚᎳᎨ ᏫᎦᏤᏓᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᏣᏛᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: yvtsatulkhe wi'ktsethst yik ski tsnuhst tsthsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: yvtsatulke wiktsetst yik ski tsnust tstsv
phrases.english_text: Would you want to go back there, to the way it was when you grew up?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏩᏚᎵᎲ ᎥᎲ ᎬᏇᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᎹᏰ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎮ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏳᏫᎨᏓ Ꮎ ᏥᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎬᏆᏘᏃᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎥᎿᎮᏃ Ᏼ ᏭᎵᏍᏙ ᏴᏓᎭ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏭᏏᏅᏌ
phrases.phonetic_text: awtulhv vhv kkwetahsti amay yki ahe elwu ywket na tsiyu khilo kkwthinhohihsti yki vnhhen y wulhsto yvtaha amay wuhsinvhsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: awtulv vv kkwetasti amay yki ae elwu ywket na tsiyu kilo kkwtinoisti yki vnen y wulsto yvtaa amay wusinvsa
phrases.english_text: Uh-huh, I do want to go back there. I could go to the water if someone would bring me in a boat, because sometimes the water edge would be right there when the water receded.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎯᎢᏛ ᏱᏣᏛᏁᏗ ᏦᎮᎮᎢᏍ ᏣᏥ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsatelkwa'v tsatahstayvhti hi'itv yitsatvnt tsohehe'ihs tstsi
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsatelkwav tsatastayvti iitv yitsatvnt tsoeeis tstsi
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎪᎨ ᎯᎦᏙᏍᏛᏭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikokhe hikathohstvwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikoke ikatostvwu
phrases.english_text: When you learned to cook, did your mom tell you, “This is how to cook”? Or did you just watch her?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᎦᏙᏍᏛᏊ ᏥᏛᏆᎴᏅᎲ ᏃᏭᏃ ᏢᏴ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗᏛ ᏃᏭ ᎥᏉᎮᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsikathohstvkw tsitvkwlenhv nown tlhvy now tsatelhohkwahsttv nowu vkwohehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsikatostvkw tsitvkwlenv nown tlvy now tsatelokwasttv nowu vkwoev
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏣᏆᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᏃᏭ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᏭᎴᏍᏊ ᏣᏪᏲᎲᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᎦᏴᎵ ᎤᏅᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: tsakwatelhohkwa'v nowu elhs tskhv nowlhskwu tsawyhohvhsk na anikayvli unvnhihstoht khuhst
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsakwatelokwav nowu els tskv nowlskwu tsawyovsk na anikayvli unvnistot kust
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏗ ᏓᏃᏎᎰ ᏗᎫᎮ ᏥᏕᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ Corn Bread ᎯᎢᏴ ᎢᏗᎩᏓ ᏥᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: toti tanohseho tikuhe tsitekohehv na khawn twat hi'iyv itikit tsitekolhskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: toti tanoseo tikue tsitekoev na kawn twat iiyv itikit tsitekolskv
phrases.english_text: When I started, I just watched her. Then a little later on I was told, "You have to learn,” then I learned. And also Grandma taught me how the elders cook things. What do they call them? They call them diguhe, cornbread. She used to make them about this [gestures] size.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏐᏩᎸᏍ
phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowlhs
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowls
phrases.english_text: Are they round?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏐᏩᎸ dog headsᎮ ᏓᏃᏎᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: anihsowal tak hathshe tanhshv
phrases.phonetic_broad: anisowal tak atse tansv
phrases.english_text: The round ones they called dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏛ
phrases.phonetic_text: v'v aklvkwtv
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv aklvkwtv
phrases.english_text: Yes, I really liked them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᎾᏅ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᏉᏢᏗ ᏣᏇᏲᏅ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏚᏯ ᎠᏑᏱ ᎦᏚ ᏃᏭᎴ ᏣᏪᏲᏅ ᎤᏖᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinanv iyuhst tikwolhvhti tskwehyonv nowl thuya ahsuy katu nowl tsaweyonv uthti
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinanv iyust tikwolvti tskweyonv nowl tuya asuy katu nowl tsaweyonv utti
phrases.english_text: She taught me how to make that kind, and she also taught me bean bread. Delicious!

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᏛ ᏥᏕᎯᏃᎮ dog heads ᎤᏗᏞᎩ ᎪᎢ ᎠᎻᏃ ᎠᏑᏴ
phrases.phonetic_text: nat tshithinohe tak haths utilhek ko'i amino ahsuyv
phrases.phonetic_broad: nat tsitinoe tak ats utilek koi amino asuyv
phrases.english_text: The dog heads you're talking about, hot grease and salt was mixed in.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ bacon grease ᎠᏑᏴᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: toyu utht tekhan kwihs ahsynv
phrases.phonetic_broad: toyu utt tekan kwis asynv
phrases.english_text: It’s really delicious, with bacon grease mixed in.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏧᏍᏆᎸᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: tshskwlte
phrases.phonetic_broad: tsskwlte
phrases.english_text: Sure is that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩᏃ ᏍᏊ ᎣᎬᏌᎮᏃ ᏦᏦᏢᏍᎬ Ꮎ butter ᏙᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᎦᏅᎵᏰᏗ Ꮎ dog heads
phrases.phonetic_text: vhskin skwu okvhshehn tsotsolhvhsk na tata tohy skwu utheht skin tikanvliyet n tak haths
phrases.phonetic_broad: vskin skwu okvsen tsotsolvsk na tata toy skwu utet skin tikanvliyet n tak ats
phrases.english_text: We also made our own butter. It was also really delicious to spread on them, the dog heads.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ Ꮭ Ᏺ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎬᏁᎸ
phrases.phonetic_text: o l yo ilhiy ski yikvnelv
phrases.phonetic_broad: o l yo iliy ski yikvnelv
phrases.english_text: I’ve never tried it that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎪᏢᏅ butter ᎤᏅᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ
phrases.phonetic_text: tyu utheht ski skwu uwhahs kolhvnhv tata unvtinv skwu
phrases.phonetic_broad: tyu utet ski skwu uwas kolvnv tata unvtinv skwu
phrases.english_text: It’s really delicious, just with butter and also cream.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎾ ᎤᎦᏗᏢᏓ creamᎢᏍ ᏣᏃᏢᏍᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: nana uhktilhvt khwimhihs tsanolhvhsk
phrases.phonetic_broad: nana uktilvt kwimis tsanolvsk
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᏊᏅ ᏕᏥᏁᎩᎡᎮ ᏩᎦ
phrases.phonetic_text: skwunv tetsineki'ehe waka
phrases.phonetic_broad: skwunv tetsinekiee waka
phrases.english_text: What about what they call cream? Did you all milk the cows?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭵ ᏙᏥᏁᎩᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᏅ cream ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬᎮᏅ cream butterᎢᏃ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎦᎾᏕᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: v ttsinek'ehv skihnv khwim skw tsikanatekvhen khwim tata'ihn skw tsikanatekv
phrases.phonetic_broad: v ttsinekev skinv kwim skw tsikanatekven kwim tatain skw tsikanatekv
phrases.english_text: Yes, we milked them. That cream too, she sold the cream and also butter.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏗᎨᏣᏙ ᏗᏣᏓᎸᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎦᏗᏍ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎢᏥᏬᏂᏍᎨ
phrases.phonetic_text: na tiketsa'to titsatalvle yik nikathihs tsalki itsiwonhihske
phrases.phonetic_broad: na tiketsato titsatalvle yik nikatis tsalki itsiwoniske
phrases.english_text: Your brothers or sisters, did you all speak Cherokee?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎦᏬᏂ ᎾᏍᏊ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏥᏬᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: na vkito kawoni nhskwu tsohsttalv nikata otsiwoni tsalki
phrases.phonetic_broad: na vkito kawoni nskwu tsosttalv nikata otsiwoni tsalki
phrases.english_text: My brother speaks and so does my sister. We all speak Cherokee.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏏᏍ ᏕᏣᏓᏩᏛᎯᏙᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: sihs tetsatawhathitho
phrases.phonetic_broad: sis tetsatawatito
phrases.english_text: Do you all still visit one another?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᏞᏍᏗ ᏗᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᏔᎵᏚ ᎢᏯᏆᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎩᎳ ᎦᏥᎪᎥ ᎠᏯ ᎥᎩᏙ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏥᏲᎵᎩ ᏱᎩ ᎰᏩ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏜ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v lhehst tikatsiko'v thaltu iykwatethiyt khil katsiko'v aya vkito etota hehst skw tsiyoliki yk howa vnh ttla
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv lest tikatsikov taltu iykwatetiyt kil katsikov aya vkito etota est skw tsiyoliki yk owa vn ttla
phrases.english_text: Uh-uh, I didn’t ever see them. I was twelve years old before I ever saw them, my dad and brother. I don’t really know him that way.

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꭳ ᏝᏕ
phrases.phonetic_text: o lthe
phrases.phonetic_broad: o lte
phrases.english_text: Oh, not really?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎲᎥ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᎦᏥᏲᎵᎩ ᏱᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: hv'v hehst how katsiyolik yki
phrases.phonetic_broad: vv est ow katsiyolik yki
phrases.english_text: No, I don’t really know them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎾ ᏕᏣᏓᏘᎿᎥ ᏣᎳᎩᏍ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ

phrases.english_text: Yes, I only knew my grandmother, my mom’s mom, and her grandma had come on the Trail of Tears. She came when she was a little girl. What she was told, Grandma told me about it. This last time we went back, I could only see shadows of the mountains. It was really bad for them, the way the Indians were treated, she told me when she [Great Grandma] was a little girl coming on that trail.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᏙᎧ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎦ ᎤᏲ ᏍᎩᎢᎦ ᎤᏲ ᏳᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏣᎾᏓᎾᏟᏍᎪ ᎤᏲ ᎨᎩᎬᏁᎵ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏝᏃ ᎠᏂᏴᏫᏯ ᏱᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᏳᏲ ᏱᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏱᎩ
phrases.phonetic_text: ltkh ski yka uyo ski'ika uy yunalhstanhel yk nkta tsantanhatlihsko uyo kkkvneli tsantiho lhano aniyvwiy yinunalhstanel yuyo yikkvnel yki
phrases.phonetic_broad: ltk ski yka uyo skiika uy yunalstanel yk nkta tsantanatlisko uyo kkkvneli tsantio lano aniyvwiy yinunalstanel yuyo yikkvnel yki
phrases.english_text: Scattered the bones and things. That’s what I think about sometimes, all these protests that they do, black people. They haven’t really had it all that bad, wanting to be helped because they’ve been treated so bad, they say. They weren’t treated as bad as the Indians.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᎾᏅ Ꮎ
phrases.phonetic_text: nika't nanv na
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikat nanv na
phrases.english_text: Everything and also… As you said, “We were chased off,” that’s what happened to them isn’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᎩᎨᎯᏙᎴ ᏣᏗ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏓᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tokkhehitole tsat skt tsnikekvnel tha
phrases.phonetic_broad: tokkeitole tsat skt tsnikekvnel ta
phrases.english_text: Everything and also… As you said, “We were chased off,” that’s what happened to them isn’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎥᏍᎩ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: vhski nkekvnle
phrases.phonetic_broad: vski nkekvnle
phrases.english_text: That's what was done to them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏂᎦᏓ ᎦᏓ ᏚᏂᎿᎡ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏎᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: nikat kta tuninha'e tunyohuhsele
phrases.phonetic_broad: nikat kta tuninae tunyousele
phrases.english_text: They lost all the land they had.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎨᏥᎩᎣᏁᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏢᏃ ᏕᎨᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎨᏥᏟᏏᏍᎨ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ Ꮎ
phrases.phonetic_text: aniyohsk ketsiki'onhele kohuhst tlvn teketsihstunhv anatho ketsitlhihsihske ikohit na
phrases.phonetic_broad: aniyosk ketsikionele koust tlvn teketsistunv anato ketsitlisiske ikoit na
phrases.english_text: The soldiers took everything from them. Somewhere they were locked up, they say, gathering them all together for that forced march. A lot of them died while they were rounded up.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏅᏓᎨᎨᏥᎢᎸᏍᏗ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᏚᏂᏲᎱᏒ ᎠᎾᏗᎲᏅ ᎨᏥᏍᏚᏅ ᏓᏂᏟᏏᏍᎬ
phrases.phonetic_text: ntakketsi'ilvhst tskwihsti skwu tuniyohuhsv anthvnhv ketsihstun tanilhihsihskv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ntakketsiilvst tskwisti skwu tuniyousv antvnv ketsistun tanilisiskv
phrases.english_text: The soldiers took everything from them. Somewhere they were locked up, they say, gathering them all together for that forced march. A lot of them died while they were rounded up.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᎮᏃ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᎬᎾᏈᏴᎰ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎤᏲ ᏂᏚᏅᏁᎴ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᎠᏯᎮᏃ ᏂᎨᎬᏁᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏁᎳᎩ ᏂᎩᎦᏛᎴᏒᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: lheno ilvhiy yikvnkwhiyvho nuhstv uyo nitunvhnl nkkvnele ayhen nikkvnle skw nelak nikikthvlehsvn tsikhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: leno ilviy yikvnkwiyvo nustv uyo nitunvnl nkkvnele ayen nikkvnle skw nelak nikiktvlesvn tsikv
phrases.english_text: They have never paid for it, what harm they caused them. What was done to them was done to us also, even though we didn’t go through it.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎢᎩᏠᏱ ᏥᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏯᏍᎩᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᏅᏓᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎤᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᎹᎹᎢᏃ ᎠᏯᏃ ᏦᎢᏁᏭᏃ ᎢᏴ
phrases.phonetic_text: ikilhoy tsnunlhstnelv ayahskinv na akeyhuhtsa ntyunhikitha elihs now tsikehv akyi ulihs kehv mam'ino ayan tso'inewhuno iyv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ikiloy tsnunlstnelv ayaskinv na akeyutsa ntyunikita elis now tsikev akyi ulis kev mamino ayan tsoinewuno iyv
phrases.english_text: It happened to our families. But us, she came when she was a girl, it was Grandma’s Grandma. And Mama and my third grandma who came as a little girl.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏏ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮎ ᏓᏳᎶᏒ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ
phrases.phonetic_text: elihs kehv skina na tayulohsv na uhsti akyhutsa
phrases.phonetic_broad: elis kev skina na tayulosv na usti akyutsa
phrases.english_text: It happened to our families. But us, she came when she was a girl, it was Grandma’s Grandma. And Mama and my third grandma who came as a little girl.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏙᏳᎭ ᎤᏲ ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᏙᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: toyuha uyo ukohvne tha
phrases.phonetic_broad: toyua uyo ukovne ta
phrases.english_text: She really saw some bad things, didn't she?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᎥᎥ
phrases.phonetic_text: ukohvne v'v
phrases.phonetic_broad: ukovne vv
phrases.english_text: Yes, she saw different things.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎩᎶ Ꮭ ᏳᏚᎵ ᎤᎪᏩᏛᏗ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᎪᎲᏁ ᎨᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: klo tl yutuli ukowahtthi iyhsti ukohvne kehsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: klo tl yutuli ukowatti iysti ukovne kesv
phrases.english_text: Someone wouldn’t want to see all the things she saw.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏲᎢᏃ ᏄᎾᎵᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏬᏚᎯᏃ ᎨᎲᎧ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏎ
phrases.phonetic_text: uyo'in nunalhstanhelv uwotuhin khehvkh skwu tsunanhikihse
phrases.phonetic_broad: uyoin nunalstanelv uwotuin kevk skwu tsunanikise
phrases.english_text: It was hard for them. Isn’t it beautiful, where they came from?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏬᏚ ᏙᎡ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᏧᎾᏂᎩᏎ

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ
phrases.phonetic_text: ohsta nuntvnhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: osta nuntvnv
phrases.english_text: They were doing well.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎮᏃ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᎭ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ Georgia Ꮎ Vann Mansion ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ
phrases.phonetic_text: naheno akhstayhvhsk katanvthha witsiyathinitahsti tsawtsa na tan manhsan tsaninhehsk
phrases.phonetic_broad: naeno akstayvsk katanvta witsiyatinitasti tsawtsa na tan mansan tsaninesk
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: VannᎮᏃ ᏭᏛ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Vann Mansion ᎤᏬᏢᎯ Jim Vann ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ
phrases.phonetic_text: tanhen wutv akhstayhvhsk skinana tan manhsan uwolhi tsim tan tuto'v skin
phrases.phonetic_broad: tanen wutv akstayvsk skinana tan mansan uwoli tsim tan tutov skin
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏅᏍ Ꮲ ᎨᏒ ᎤᎾᏓᏂᏴᏓ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᏝᏃ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ Ꮩ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏎᏅ ᎠᏆᏚᎵᏭ ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏂᏓᏍᏗ
phrases.phonetic_text: skinvhs lhv kehsv unta'niyhvht'a anatho tln yawanvth to yiki ahsenhv akwtuliw witsiyathinitahsti
phrases.phonetic_broad: skinvs lv kesv untaniyvta anato tln yawanvt to yiki asenv akwtuliw witsiyatinitasti
phrases.english_text: My wife, I’m thinking about taking her there to Georgia. Vann Mansion, they talk about, Vann was my wife’s last name. Jim Vann owned Vann Mansion. Somewhere there they were left behind they say, her relatives. I don’t know for sure; I just want to take her there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎡᎵᏛ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏂ ᎬᎿ ᏚᎾᏂᎩᏒ
phrases.phonetic_text: elit ytvwhath khuhst tsuwanhi khvnha tunanikhsv
phrases.phonetic_broad: elit ytvwat kust tsuwani kvna tunaniksv
phrases.english_text: You might be able to find some of her relatives there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎪᏪᎵᏴ ᏯᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙᎳ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ
phrases.phonetic_text: kwheliy yahstawatitola elw ytwhatha
phrases.phonetic_broad: kweliy yastawatitola elw ytwata
phrases.english_text: If you follow the written records, you can find them.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᎮᏃ Ꮎ last name ᎨᎲ ᎠᏂSwimmerᎮᏃ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᎷᏥᏝ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎯᎠ ᎢᏳᎾᏍᏗ Ꮭ Ꮟ ᏱᏗᏁᎮ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᎦᏓ ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayhen na wahst nem khv anihswimmhen kehv uniluhtsil skina hi'a iyunhsti lha si ytinehe eliwu yikat tsunto'ita
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayen na wast nem kv aniswimmen kev unilutsil skina ia iyunsti la si ytinee eliwu yikat tsuntoita
phrases.english_text: For me, our last name was Swimmer, when they got here. The ones with this name weren’t still living there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ᏺ ᎠᏆᏅᏔ Ᏺ Ꮎ North Carolina ᎨᎲ Perry Shell ᏚᏙᎠ ᏤᎭ Ᏺ ᎣᎦᏅᏔ Ᏺ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏦᎬᏂ
phrases.phonetic_text: aytv yo akwanth yo nha nawt khawawana kehv thawi hsaw tuto'a tseha yo oknvtha y khuhst tsokvni
phrases.phonetic_broad: aytv yo akwant yo na nawt kawawana kev tawi saw tutoa tsea yo oknvta y kust tsokvni
phrases.english_text: For me, I know in North Carolina, Perry Shell his name. We know we’re family.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎤᏖᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎬᏕᎶᎰᎯᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᎨᎵᎰ
phrases.phonetic_text: uthti yik kvtelhohihsti yik kliho
phrases.phonetic_broad: utti yik kvteloisti yik klio
phrases.english_text: I think it’s really amazing to be able to find out.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎭᎳᏛᏴ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᏙᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: halatvyv ytvwhath tha
phrases.phonetic_broad: alatvyv ytvwat ta
phrases.english_text: You can find out a lot, ain’t it?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᏱᏛᏩᏔ ᏥᏈᏍᏗᎡ ᏗᏁᎭ
phrases.phonetic_text: tskwihst ythvwath tskw'ihsti'e tineha
phrases.phonetic_broad: tskwist ytvwat tskwistie tinea
phrases.english_text: You can find a lot. There’s a lot living there.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏃ Marble City ᏣᏛᎦᏅ Ꮎ Marble City
phrases.phonetic_text: ayan mawtaw hsiti tstkn na mawtaw hsiti
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayan mawtaw siti tstkn na mawtaw siti
phrases.english_text: For me, Marble City, you’ve heard of Marble City? If somebody died over there, that’s your family, they’d say. I didn’t know anything about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎦᏓᏲᏍᏗ ᎩᎶᏕ ᏱᏧᏲᎱᏌ ᎥᎿ ᎫᏍᏕᏍ ᏱᎬᏁᏗ ᏯᎾᏓ ᎾᏆᏅᏛᏂ ᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: katayohsti khilote yitsuyohuhsa vnh kuhstehs yikvhnti yant nkwntni kehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: katayosti kilote yitsuyousa vn kustes yikvnti yant nkwntni kev
phrases.english_text: For me, Marble City, you’ve heard of Marble City? If somebody died over there, that’s your family, they’d say. I didn’t know anything about that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏂᎦᏥᏪᎮᎸ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏓᎾᏛᏍᎬ ᎥᎿ Dry Creek ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏗᏣᎦᏎᏍᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎥᎿ ᏗᏁᎲ ᏂᎦᏗᏍ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᏨᏂ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ ᎣᏏᏃ ᎤᏃᎯᏳᏁ Ꮩ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎾᏛᏁᎴ
phrases.phonetic_text: skin nikatsiwhelv anitshuths tanthskv vnh twa khwikh hehsti ytitsakhsehstihehsti anikyutsa vnh tinehv nikatihs kohuhst ttsn ktsyhehv ohsino unohiyne to lha ski ynntnele
phrases.phonetic_broad: skin nikatsiwelv anitsuts tantskv vn twa kwik esti ytitsaksestiesti anikyutsa vn tinev nikatis koust ttsn ktsyev osino unoiyne to la ski ynntnele
phrases.english_text: That’s what I told my boys growing up in Dry Creek. “Don’t look for girls over there, you’re related to everybody”. They really believed it; they didn’t do that.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏣᏛᎦᏅᏅᎮ ᏍᏊ Greasy ᏣᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎥᎿᏭ ᎠᏗᏜᏴ Kentucky ᎠᏃᎮᎭᎮᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: ayt na akhstayhvhsk tstvknvnhe skw kwihsi tsaninhehskv vnhawu atilyv khantakhi anohehahen tskhv
phrases.phonetic_broad: ayt na akstayvsk tstvknvne skw kwisi tsanineskv vnawu atilyv kantaki anoeaen tskv
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. Were you able to help, were you old enough to help?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏍᎩᏃ ᏲᎩᏃᎮᏝ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏋᏂ ᏱᎩ Kentucky ᏫᏥᏯᏅᎲ ᎠᎩᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: skin yoknohel tlha khuhsti akwvn yik khantakhi witsiynhv akhstayhvhski ktsiyohehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: skin yoknoel tla kusti akwvn yik kantaki witsiynv akstayvski ktsiyoev
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. Were you able to help, were you old enough to help?

phrases.syllabary_text: Ꮎ ᏥᏂᏃᎲᎳ ᏙᏗᏣᏛᏏᏙᎸ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᏙᏥᎯᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎡᎵᏍ ᎦᏣᎵᏍᏕᎸᏗ ᏱᏣᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ
phrases.phonetic_text: n tsninohvl totitsathvhsitolv na sihkw totsihihv tsatihv elihs katslhstelt yitsatethiyvt khe nhiyu
phrases.phonetic_broad: n tsninovl totitsatvsitolv na sikw totsiiv tsativ elis katslstelt yitsatetiyvt ke niyu
phrases.english_text: As for me, my wife, you’ve heard of Greasy, that they were talking about? There on the other side, used to be what they call Kentucky. If we talk about things like that, I will say we’re not related, I married her from Kentucky, my wife I told them… Let’s talk about how you all grew up. We killed hogs, you said. Were you able to help, were you old enough to help?

phrases.syllabary_text: ᏝᏍᏊ Ꮩ Ꮞ ᎡᎵ ᎠᏆᏍᏗᎩ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏳᎳᏅ Ꭱ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᎲᏒᏅ ᎦᎳᏅᏓᏕ Ᏺ ᎡᎵ ᎠᏆᎵᏍᏕᎸᏗ ᎨᎲ
phrases.phonetic_text: lhahskwu to se eli akwhstik kehv kayulnv e kohuhsti ahvhsvnhv kalnvtat yo eli akwalhstelthi kehv
phrases.phonetic_broad: laskwu to se eli akwstik kev kayulnv e kousti avsvnv kalnvtat yo eli akwalstelti kev
phrases.english_text: Not really, I was probably too little. Things had already been moved when I was able to help. She had what they called a smoke house, where she stored the meat. She would hang the meat and then she would rub salt on it and that’s how she would preserve the meat.

phrases.syllabary_text: ᎾᎮᏃ ᏗᎦᏒᏍᏗ ᏥᎪᎮᎲ Ꮎ smoke house ᏧᏓᏁᎸ ᎥᎿ ᏣᏍᏆᏂᎪᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎭᏫᏯ
phrases.phonetic_text: nahen tikhsvhsti tsikohehv n hsmokh hahs tstanelv vnh tsahskwankothv n hawiya

When it was boiling, the bucket would go like this [gestures]. She said it was following the movement of the heart. The bucket went like that [gestures] as she poured the water in. And then when she was boiling it, on the seventh time, she would leave some for her to drink. If someone was ill, there are many different kinds. I forget sometimes and then when I really think about it, I remember it.

phrases.english_text: They are trying. I go to Tulsa, and I go here in town. When it gets worse, I go to Tulsa, when they can’t help me here. It started as glaucoma. They didn’t know what it was here at first, when it started. Something happened inside and they couldn’t fix it. One time we went to Crosslin, a healer that lived in Sallisaw. And he took me to water. Really a wonder what happened then, the way my eyes are now, I can’t see anything. It’s just white is all I see in here. I can’t see you two. That’s the way they were when we got there. He told me what I needed was to go to water, so that’s what he did, he took me to water. And when my husband and I left, as we got on the road and past the stomp grounds, my eye started itching. So, I closed my eyes and rubbed my eye, and when I opened them, I could see, just that quick it was good, he healed me. He was a real good healer; I was able to see for a long time after that. My husband, something happened to his heart then at the time. I was sitting up too much at night, I couldn’t sleep; that’s when it started. My eyesight got weak or fading, but not all of it faded out. I could still see a bit. Then five years ago, suddenly I lost my eyesight, but I still have hope.

phrases.english_text: That’s how it was sometimes when people were around, they would tell stories. What happened in the past, and then at night she started telling me things until I was asleep. She talked about a lot of things that her grandma had told her. Where we were, they talked a little bit about what they call Juhlgal. It’s something tall. How Grandma described it to me was a little different, but there was one thing she used to talk about. There was a tree, and the women, there were these beans that grew back then, they would go up the mountain looking for where those beans grew, to cook them. About halfway up, they were sitting down when something started making a sound. When they looked up there, there was something standing between the tree branches. The girl said there was something tall in between the branches, it looked like a star she said, Grandma said. When we were there in the valley where they had been, I didn’t go. It was too rough for me to go, I was told. They were saying there were markings, something that Juhlgal had done. They said those markings, no one can read what it’s saying. They said when they went, some of them went to look at it. They say that Juhlgal had done that, they were saying.

phrases.english_text: Yes, she told me a lot of things. And the Indians that were there, they danced, and one time they were saying if a panther was coming it would howl. If a panther was coming, they would stay behind to build fires at the dance ground, because the panther was afraid of fire. One time they left behind a blind old woman, she was staying at their home. She could hear the panther growling as it was coming near. The old woman didn’t know what she was going to do. “When it finds out I am in here, it will come eat me,” the old woman thought. So, she heated up some water, bringing it to a boil. Sure enough, the panther came in. The houses that they lived in were like tents covered in tree leaves, and when it opened the woman sat there, and did this [gestures] to the panther. When it opened, the panther was splashed with hot water, and it ran off, backing away because it had been scalded. The next morning, the dancers returned, and the panther wasn’t there. It was hurt too badly, and so the dancers had to go kill it.

phrases.english_text: They were bad. One time she said, “This man’s wife was running around on him. So, she went to a dance and left the boy to stay with his grandma.” I think they were staying with her. “Let her go,” Grandma told the boy when the wife left. She didn’t take much of her things. The old woman sat in front of the fireplace and put all she had down. And there, the boy saw she had laid out some arrowheads. She had hung what they call a moccasin––you know the kind made out of deer skin––she hung it in front of where she had the arrowheads. Later on, she left and one of the arrowheads made a sound, so she went to where the bundle was on the chimney. Later on, when she came back, she said to the flint, “You didn’t do anything.” So then she sent another arrowhead and again when it came back it hadn’t done anything. “You didn’t go do anything either,” she said to it. Then she put it away. When the third one left and came back she had a container this [gestures] size with water, and the arrowhead went into it. It was washed, and the arrowhead had blood on it. “You really did something,” she said to it, then she put it up. Later on, someone came and told the boy that his wife had died at the dance. The flint must have shot her.

phrases.english_text: Another one? Let's see… because there’s a lot of things I know. Also, the Ukten that they talk about, have you all heard of it? One time she said they went fishing. Standing Rock, as they call it, by Oklahoma Station, near where the river is. Standing Rock, as they called it, because Grandma said a rock used to stand there. It’s underwater. These days the water isn’t as deep as she was saying around that area. There, a tree that had fallen was there. Grandma would sit on it before others started coming to fish there in the deep end. Long dresses, they wore back then. Her dress was in the way of her fishing. After a while something was moving below, she saw it and looked. It looked like a cow. It was looking at her from below. It was kind of like a greenish color, she said. Its eyes were like a cow, and its nose too, and it had horns. She watched it, she thought, “What am I going to do?” The others fishing there, she didn’t want to yell at them. “Let’s get down for a little while,” she told them, walking away. “Let’s get down for a while”. They all started walking back. They didn’t ask why when they were told to get off. When they went up a little further, she told them, and that’s when they started running, she said. That was Ukten, she used to say. That’s where it lives, she used to say, in the deep end of the water, there near Standing Rock. I think there are still some things that are living in the deep end of the water.

phrases.english_text: One time we took the kids there, it really was dangerous because I didn't know how to swim. We took them, and Sam, that you said, he’s not living now, he was killed by a car. It was hard for him to mind; he was going towards the deep. “Come back, come back,” I was saying. Over here were the other kids. He was still going and the younger boy got out, and we were calling him to come back. He’d just giggle. After a while something came up behind him, and he was facing us. It came up so far, it was like a snake and was this [gestures] big. Pretty big. It had eyes when it came up. That’s when I started hollering “Come here, come here!” I was telling him. That girl too, she started jumping around. “Come back!” Then the boy started to run back. All of a sudden, it came up, that thing like a snake. Not too long after, my husband was working at Six Shooter, somebody came there in a boat. He said someone there saw a big snake-like thing floating in the water, they said, below that rock bluff. I didn’t know what it was, but it was pretty long. Something like a snake it was, that the others had seen.

He was still going and the younger boy got out, and we were calling him to come back. He’d just giggle. After a while something came up behind him, and he was facing us. It came up so far, it was like a snake and was this [gestures] big. Pretty big. It had eyes when it came up. That’s when I started hollering “Come here, come here!” I was telling him. That girl too, she started jumping around. “Come back!” Then the boy started to run back. All of a sudden, it came up, that thing like a snake. Not too long after, my husband was working at Six Shooter, somebody came there in a boat. He said someone there saw a big snake-like thing floating in the water, they said, below that rock bluff. I didn’t know what it was, but it was pretty long. Something like a snake it was, that the others had seen.

phrases.english_text: That too, little people. She used to tell me about them. I never experienced that, but my daughter experienced it once. phrases.english_text: Yes, those too. She told one about when they were taking care of a sick person, the medicine man was doctoring them and couldn’t cure them. Then someone checked. A raven is disturbing this one. They can’t get better unless it takes them, she was told. Unless you get somebody brave and young. You get them, tonight this doorway on both sides they will sit, because the raven will come back, they were told. There were two brave young men. “We will do it!” they said. They used medicine on them and were seated next to the doorway. Back then when somebody was sick, people would come, they would be outside and have a fire going, that’s how they were. The young men that were treated with medicine heard something in the distance. They had been told what was going to happen. They were waiting on it. The second time they heard the noise it was a little closer, and a third, and a fourth, and then on the steps landed a beautiful woman. She wore a long knife on her side, as she walked, she didn’t see the boys watching over the sick person. When the woman got to the doorway, the boys grabbed her. She was very strong, I think. She almost got away from the young boys. She was slinging them around, but they held on to her until morning came. That morning, when it got light out, they let her go. The woman was naked. The dress she had was covered in corn and it broke and left her naked. I don’t know if she lived close by or not. Nobody heard anything about anyone passing away, because she was going to die when she got home, they were told. But they didn’t hear anything. I guess she must’ve lived too far away. Then the sick person began to get better. That’s what was coming to the sickly person, that raven demon.
